title: Memorandum on Good Faith Estimate Settings for the Patient Financial Account
content:
A Good Faith Estimate is the No Surprises Act uninsured or self-pay estimate issued for scheduled services. For each financial class of the Patient Financial Account the group sets whether a Good Faith Estimate must be issued; the amount by which the billed total for an encounter must exceed its Good Faith Estimate for the patient to be eligible for the billed-versus-estimate dispute; the calendar days after the date of the first bill for the encounter within which that dispute may be started; and the business days within which the estimate is delivered, one figure for a service scheduled 3 to 9 business days ahead and another for a service scheduled 10 or more business days ahead.

| Financial class (tier) | Estimate required | Dispute threshold (USD) | Dispute window (calendar days) | Delivery, booked 3–9 business days ahead (business days) | Delivery, booked 10 or more business days ahead (business days) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Medicaid Managed Care Account | no | 0.00 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Self-Pay Account | yes | 400.00 | 120 | 1 | 3 |
| Medicare Part B Account | no | 0.00 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Medicare Advantage Account | no | 0.00 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Commercial HMO/EPO Account | no | 0.00 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Commercial PPO/POS Account | no | 0.00 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| High-Deductible Health Plan Account | no | 0.00 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

The Self-Pay Account is the one class on which an estimate is required. Its dispute threshold is 400.00, its dispute window 120 calendar days, and its estimate is delivered within 1 business day for a service booked 3 to 9 business days ahead and within 3 business days for a service booked 10 or more business days ahead. Every insured class shows zero in each figure.
